taxa.name: Australopithecus prometheus (debated)
taxa.meaning: Proposed second southern African australopith species revived for StW 573 ('Little Foot') and large-toothed Makapansgat/Sterkfontein specimens; most specialists fold these into Australopithecus africanus.
taxa.note: Dart coined A. prometheus in 1948 for Makapansgat; Ronald Clarke and collaborators apply it to StW 573 and parts of Sterkfontein Members 2–4, whereas Beaudet and others retain single-species variation in A. africanus.

evidence.title: Lothagam (Apak / Nawata, West Turkana, Kenya): KNM-LT 329 cf. A. anamensis
evidence.dateBasis: Tephrostratigraphy (basal Apak Member / Upper Nawata) & mammalian biochronology
evidence.summary: The KNM-LT 329 right mandibular corpus fragment with M1 (discovered 1967) and isolated teeth represent one of the earliest post-Miocene East African hominins bridging Ardipithecus/late Miocene forms and Australopithecus anamensis in the southwestern Turkana Basin.
evidence.limits: Fragmentary specimen; debated between late Miocene cf. Ardipithecus/Orrorin affinity and earliest cf. Australopithecus anamensis.

evidence.title: Tabarin (Chemeron Formation, Tugen Hills, Kenya): KNM-TH 13150 mandible
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar single-crystal laser-fusion tuff dating in the Baringo/Tugen Hills sequence
evidence.summary: Right mandibular fragment with heavily worn M1–M2 recovered at Tabarin in the Baringo Basin; variably assigned to Ardipithecus ramidus or cf. Australopithecus anamensis right around the Pliocene origin of Australopithecus.
evidence.limits: Single partial mandible without anterior dentition; generic assignment (Ardipithecus vs Australopithecus) remains debated.

evidence.title: Ileret Area 8 (East Turkana, Kenya): 4.3 Ma Australopithecus anamensis mandible
evidence.dateBasis: Tephrostratigraphy beneath the 4.2 Ma Moiti / Lonyumun Member horizons at Ileret
evidence.summary: A 4.3-million-year-old Australopithecus anamensis mandible described by Lewis, Ward & colleagues (2024) from Ileret, extending the Turkana Basin record of A. anamensis slightly earlier than Kanapoi and documenting wooded-to-bushland paleoenvironments.
evidence.limits: Single mandibular specimen; illustrates how scarce ~4.3 Ma fluvial exposures are prior to the Kanapoi deltaic sequence.

evidence.title: Asa Issie & Aramis (Middle Awash, Ethiopia): 4.2–4.1 Ma Australopithecus anamensis
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar tuff correlation above the 4.4 Ma Aramis Ardipithecus ramidus beds
evidence.summary: Over 30 A. anamensis specimens (ASI-VP-2/2 maxilla/dentition, femur shaft, foot phalanx) stratified directly above 4.4 Ma Ardipithecus ramidus in the Middle Awash, evidencing an evolutionary shift to thicker enamel, buttressed jaws, and open-woodland foraging.
evidence.limits: Debated whether the stratigraphic succession Ar. ramidus → A. anamensis at Middle Awash represents direct local anagenesis or replacement/dispersal.

evidence.title: Fejej FJ-4 (South Omo, Ethiopia): 4.18–4.0 Ma Australopithecus anamensis teeth
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of overlying basalts capping the FJ-4 fossiliferous sand
evidence.summary: Five associated mandibular teeth (FJ-4-SB-1 to 5) recovered north of the Kenyan border in southern Ethiopia, matching Kanapoi and Asa Issie Australopithecus anamensis dental proportions.
evidence.limits: Originally provisionally compared with A. afarensis before A. anamensis was formally named in 1995; isolated teeth lack cranial context.

evidence.title: Galili (Somali Region, Southern Afar, Ethiopia): ~4.2–3.9 Ma early Australopithecus
evidence.dateBasis: Basalt 40Ar/39Ar geochronology & Pliocene suid/proboscidean biochronology
evidence.summary: Dental remains and proximal femur fragments from the Mount Galili Formation on the southeastern Afar margin, documenting early Pliocene Australopithecus across lake-margin and woodland habitats south of the main Awash sites.
evidence.limits: Sample consists mainly of isolated teeth and postcranial fragments spanning multiple volcaniclastic members.

evidence.title: Allia Bay Area 261 (East Turkana, Kenya): 3.97 Ma Australopithecus anamensis paratypes
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of the Moiti Tuff immediately overlying the fossil-bearing bonebed
evidence.summary: Over two dozen craniodental and postcranial specimens (KNM-ER 30200 maxilla, radius, teeth) from Allia Bay on the east shore of Lake Turkana, forming the paratype hypodigm alongside Kanapoi for naming A. anamensis (Leakey et al. 1995).
evidence.limits: Fluvial deltaic channel concentration mixes remains across a narrow stratigraphic horizon beneath the Moiti Tuff.

evidence.title: Belohdelie (Middle Awash, Ethiopia): 3.89 Ma BEL-VP-1/1 frontal bone
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of the Cindery Tuff (~3.85 Ma) and adjacent basalt/tuffs in the Sagantole Formation
evidence.summary: Partial frontal cranium (BEL-VP-1/1) preserving supraorbital brow and frontal squama morphology closely aligning with Australopithecus afarensis during its temporal transition/overlap with late A. anamensis (MRD at 3.8 Ma).
evidence.limits: Lacks associated dentition, making unambiguous species-level separation between earliest A. afarensis and latest A. anamensis inferential.

evidence.title: Laetoli & Garusi (Northern Tanzania): LH 4 holotype mandible & Garusi 1 maxilla
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of Tuff 7 (3.66 Ma) and Lower/Upper Laetolil Beds volcanic ashes
evidence.summary: Beside the Site G and Site S footprint trails, Laetoli yielded Garusi 1 (1939 Kohl-Larsen maxilla) and Mary Leakey's 1974–1979 Upper Laetolil skeletal/dental series including LH 4 — the designated holotype mandible of Australopithecus afarensis — plus LH 21 juvenile skeleton and Site A's enigmatic 2021 cross-stepping trackway.
evidence.limits: Site A tracks (McNutt et al. 2021) differ markedly in foot kinematics from Site G, suggesting more than one bipedal hominin at Laetoli.

evidence.title: Woranso-Mille Korsi Dora (Afar, Ethiopia): KSD-VP-1/1 ('Kadanuumuu') partial skeleton
evidence.dateBasis: Single-crystal 40Ar/39Ar ash dating and paleomagnetic reversal stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Partial large adult skeleton (~1.5–1.6 m tall) KSD-VP-1/1 ('Kadanuumuu', meaning 'big man'), preserving scapula, ribs, clavicle, pelvis, tibia, and arm bones 400 kyr older than Lucy, demonstrating full committed terrestrial stride geometry early in A. afarensis.
evidence.limits: Lacks cranium and feet; reveals stronger sexual dimorphism / larger male stature than expected from Hadar's Lucy alone.

evidence.title: Koro Toro KT 13 & KT 40 (Bahr el Ghazal, Chad): Additional West-Central A. bahrelghazali sites
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic 10Be/9Be sediment nuclide dating & biochronological fauna correlation
evidence.summary: Companion localities to KT 12 ('Abel') in the Bahr el Ghazal basin (~2,500 km west of the East African Rift), yielding additional dental/gnathic remains and C4 savanna-wetland isotope signatures proving sustained Pliocene hominin occupation of Central Africa.
evidence.limits: Sparse isolated material; some specialists treat A. bahrelghazali as a western geographic variant of A. afarensis rather than a separate species.

evidence.title: Kantis Fossil Site (Ongata Rongai, Nairobi Margin, Kenya): KNM-KN highland A. afarensis
evidence.dateBasis: K-Ar/40Ar-39Ar volcanic tuff dating & Pliocene mammalian biochronology
evidence.summary: First Australopithecus afarensis locality discovered on the elevated eastern shoulder of the Kenya Rift Valley near Nairobi (~1,740 m modern elevation), yielding KNM-KN 46421 forearm ulna and teeth and demonstrating that australopiths thrived outside hot, low Rift lake basins.
evidence.limits: Small hominin sample size (proximal ulna, juvenile/adult teeth) compared with lowland Afar research areas.

evidence.title: Woranso-Mille Leado Dido'a & Mesgid Dora (Afar, Ethiopia): Mid-Pliocene Australopithecus
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar volcanic tuff correlation across the Woranso-Mille fault blocks
evidence.summary: Craniodental and postcranial finds reported by Melillo et al. (2021) and Haile-Selassie et al. (2025) from Leado Dido'a and Mesgid Dora, confirming that up to three distinct hominin adaptive lineages coexisted around one Central Afar river-delta system 3.5–3.3 million years ago.
evidence.limits: Some fragmentary remains from Leado Dido'a cannot yet be assigned with certainty between A. afarensis and A. deyiremeda.

evidence.title: Chemeron Formation Localities (Baringo Basin, Kenya): Mid-Pliocene Australopithecus teeth
evidence.dateBasis: Pliocene biochronology and Chemeron Formation tephrostratigraphy
evidence.summary: Additional mid-Pliocene hominid molars/premolar specimens documented by Pickford, Senut & colleagues (2022) from Baringo County, linking Kenya's Central Rift to contemporary Ethiopian Afar and Turkana australopith populations.
evidence.limits: Isolated teeth; species-level assignment between A. afarensis, Kenyanthropus, and A. deyiremeda-grade hominins remains open.

evidence.title: Maka (Middle Awash, Ethiopia): 3.4 Ma MAK-VP-1/12 mandible & humerus
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of the Sidi Hakoma Tuff / Maka sand unit
evidence.summary: Key early-to-mid-sequence A. afarensis collection (MAK-VP-1/12 complete mandible, femur, humerus, ulna) proving morphological unity between Tanzanian Laetoli (~3.66 Ma) and Ethiopian Hadar (~3.2 Ma) populations across nearly 1,800 km.
evidence.limits: Concentrated within a single fluvial horizon; reinforces intraspecific variation debate in A. afarensis.

evidence.title: Hadar Locality AL 129 (Sidi Hakoma Member, Ethiopia): 3.4 Ma bipedal knee joint
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar Sidi Hakoma Tuff (3.42 Ma) & Denen Dora stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Discovered in October 1973 a year before Lucy, the AL 129-1 distal femur and proximal tibia demonstrated an unmistakably human-like bicondylar valgus knee angle in a small ~3.4 Ma Pliocene hominin, proving bipedalism preceded brain expansion by >1.5 Myr.
evidence.limits: Single partial knee joint from a juvenile/small adult; taxonomy awaited the broader AL 333 and Laetoli A. afarensis naming in 1978.

evidence.title: Hadar AL 333 ('First Family') & AL 444-2 (Ethiopia): 3.2–3.0 Ma A. afarensis population
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar Kadar Hadar Member tuffs (BKT-2, Kada Hadar Tuff 3.20 Ma)
evidence.summary: AL 333 yielded >240 bones of at least 17 individuals (adults and juveniles) deposited rapidly in one sheetflood channel ~3.2 Ma, while nearby AL 444-2 (3.0 Ma) preserves the most complete adult male A. afarensis skull, constraining cranial variation and sexual dimorphism.
evidence.limits: Whether AL 333 represents a single social group caught in a flash flood or time-averaged accumulation remains discussed, though deposition was geologically brief.

evidence.title: Koobi Fora Lokochot & Tulu Bor Members (East Turkana, Kenya): ~3.4–3.0 Ma Australopithecus
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of Tulu Bor Tuff (3.44 Ma) & Lokochot tephra correlations
evidence.summary: Rare mid-Pliocene cranial and dental fragments (including KNM-ER 2602 temporal/parietal fragments and Area 117/129/204 specimens) documenting Australopithecus presence in East Turkana contemporaneous with West Turkana Lomekwi Kenyanthropus.
evidence.limits: High morphological fragmentation makes some mid-Pliocene East Turkana fossils ambiguous between A. afarensis and Kenyanthropus.

evidence.title: Omo Usno & Shungura Members A–B (Lower Omo Valley, Ethiopia): 3.6–2.95 Ma Australopithecus
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar dating of Tuffs U-10, A, B, and C across the Shungura master section
evidence.summary: Isolated Australopithecus molars and premolars (e.g., W-752, L-1, Omo 28) from the lower Shungura and Usno formations bridging the Pliocene transition before Paranthropus aethiopicus and early Homo appear above Tuff C (~2.95 Ma).
evidence.limits: Almost exclusively isolated teeth due to high-energy braided-river transport.

evidence.title: Ledi-Geraru Gurumaha & Lee Adoyta (Afar, Ethiopia): 2.8–2.6 Ma late Australopithecus
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar Gurumaha & Lee Adoyta volcanic tuff tephrochronology
evidence.summary: Ten new hominin teeth reported by Villmoare et al. (2025, Nature) at ~2.78 and ~2.59 Ma proving that a late-surviving, previously undescribed non-afarensis species of Australopithecus directly overlapped in space and time with the earliest Homo (LD 350-1) in the Afar.
evidence.limits: Dental specimens are morphologically distinct from A. afarensis and A. garhi but not yet formally named as a new species.

evidence.title: Sterkfontein Jacovec Cavern (Gauteng, South Africa): StW 578 partial cranium & clavicle
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic 26Al/10Be burial dating of quartz breccia vs paleomagnetic/faunal correlation
evidence.summary: Deep chamber in the Sterkfontein cave system yielding the StW 578 partial cranium, clavicle, and limb bones; cosmogenic burial dates (~3.76 Ma) challenge faunal/U-Pb estimates by suggesting hominins entered southern African caves earlier than previously accepted.
evidence.limits: Intensely debated whether cosmogenic nuclide burial ages reflect original sediment entry (~3.76 Ma) or reworked pre-buried chert.

evidence.title: Sterkfontein Member 2 Silberberg Grotto (South Africa): StW 573 'Little Foot' skeleton
evidence.dateBasis: Isochron 26Al/10Be burial dating (~3.67 Ma) vs flowstone U-Pb (~2.8–2.2 Ma) & biochronology
evidence.summary: At >90% anatomical completeness, StW 573 ('Little Foot', an elderly adult female excavated over 20 years from dolomitic breccia by Ronald Clarke) is the most complete Australopithecus skeleton known, preserving both ape-like grasping hallux capability and modern human-like lower-limb proportions.
evidence.limits: Two major disputes: age (~3.67 Ma cosmogenic/biochronology vs ~2.2–2.8 Ma younger flowstone/reworking models) and taxonomy (A. prometheus vs A. africanus).

evidence.title: Sterkfontein Member 4 (Gauteng, South Africa): Sts 5 ('Mrs. Ples'), Sts 14 & >500 A. africanus
evidence.dateBasis: 26Al/10Be cosmogenic nuclides (Granger 2022) vs flowstone U-Pb & cercopithecid biochronology (Frost 2022)
evidence.summary: Richest single Australopithecus assemblage on Earth (>500 specimens across decades of work by Broom, Robinson, Tobias & Clarke), including Sts 5 ('Mrs. Ples'), Sts 14 pelvis/spine, Sts 71, StW 505, and StW 431, plus 2025 enamel palaeoproteomics confirming A. africanus sex/peptide fidelity.
evidence.limits: Stratigraphic/chronological battleground: Granger et al. (2022) date Member 4 breccias to ~3.4–3.6 Ma while Frost et al. (2022) & flowstone U-Pb date them to ~2.8–2.0 Ma.

evidence.title: Gladysvale Cave (Gauteng, South Africa): 2.4–2.0 Ma Australopithecus africanus teeth
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, paleomagnetism & flowstone U-series/U-Pb stratigraphy
evidence.summary: Recognized in 1992 by Lee Berger and Phillip Tobias as the first new Australopithecus cave discovered in the Cradle of Humankind in 44 years, yielding A. africanus teeth (GVH-1, GVH-2) and calcified cave deposits spanning Early–Middle Pleistocene cycles.
evidence.limits: Hominin fossils derive mostly from ex-situ miner's dumps alongside stratified internal breccias.

evidence.title: Sterkfontein Member 5 / StW 53 Infill (South Africa): ~2.2–1.7 Ma late A. africanus / early Homo
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic nuclide burial & U-Pb flowstone constraints
evidence.summary: Crushed StW 53 cranium and Oldowan-bearing Member 5 East deposits marking the late Pliocene–Early Pleistocene boundary at Sterkfontein, variably attributed to terminal A. africanus or earliest South African Homo habilis.
evidence.limits: Complex karst collapse and infill boundaries caused decades of debate over StW 53's taxonomic status and association with Oldowan tools.

waves.title: Early Australopithecus Rift Origin Corridor (Turkana–Afar)
waves.summary: Schematic East African Rift corridor linking earliest 4.3–4.1 Ma Australopithecus anamensis habitats across Turkana (Kanapoi, Ileret, Allia Bay), Fejej, and the Middle Awash (Asa Issie).
waves.limits: Schematic envelope reflecting preserved volcano-sedimentary Rift basins rather than a complete ancestral range.

waves.title: Mid-Pliocene Australopithecus afarensis & Contemporary Expansion
waves.summary: Nearly 1-million-year Rift distribution of A. afarensis from the Afar Depression (Hadar, Dikika, Woranso-Mille, Maka) across high Rift shoulders (Kantis) to northern Tanzania (Laetoli), coexisting alongside A. deyiremeda and Kenyanthropus.
waves.limits: Connecting preserved outcrops omits intervening Kenyan/Tanzanian highland corridors where erosion removed Pliocene strata.

waves.title: Trans-Saharan Mega-Lake Chad Pliocene Dispersal (to Koro Toro)
waves.summary: Pliocene humid gallery-savanna corridor enabling Australopithecus populations (A. bahrelghazali) to inhabit the Lake Chad basin 2,500 km west of East Africa.
waves.limits: Intervening Sudan/Chadian savannahs lack exposed 3.6 Ma outcrops, leaving exact migration timing and direction schematic.

waves.title: East-to-Southern Africa Australopithecus Savanna Corridor
waves.summary: Pliocene–Early Pleistocene wooded-savanna woodland corridor linking East African Rift populations through the Malawi/Luangwa Rift to South African dolomitic caves (Makapansgat, Sterkfontein, Gladysvale, Taung, and late Malapa A. sediba).
waves.limits: Almost all southern African sites are dolomitic cave infills rather than Rift lake beds, biasing preservation toward karst uplands.

studies.title: Australopithecus: Every Published Fossil Locality Across Africa (~5.0–1.98 Ma)
studies.summary: Complete geographic and chronological atlas of 39 published Australopithecus fossil localities and stratigraphic horizons across East, Central (Chad), and Southern Africa—from cf. A. anamensis at Lothagam and 4.3 Ma Ileret through A. afarensis, A. deyiremeda, A. bahrelghazali, A. garhi, A. africanus / Little Foot, to 1.98 Ma A. sediba at Malapa.
